absent: Numeric values for ioctl commands, clone tags, magic numbers, handle kinds and error codes.
Internal layout and locking for namespace common, mount, pid, user and other per type structures beyond observed fields.
Implementation of stashed path materialization, dentry pruning, sequential mount selection and tree lookup.
Reference counting transitions for active versus passive references and global mount lifetime.
Credential handling, user namespace translation, and broad visibility privilege evaluation.
File descriptor allocation, publishing, and file opening mechanics for namespace paths.
Pipe buffer operations, occupancy arithmetic, wait queue behavior and async notification delivery.
Configuration gating for optional namespace types and version evolution of mount info and handle formats.
Superblock and inode helpers such as statistics, clearing, and pseudofilesystem setup beyond wiring observed.
Signal handling and scheduling interactions during splice waits beyond abort and reschedule points shown.

findings.text: Path resolution for namespaces is available through a callback form that takes a helper plus opaque data and through a task form that takes a destination path with a task and type operations, reporting not found when no namespace is returned.
Opening services consume a namespace reference to produce a close on exec read only descriptor, with a related form that first resolves a relative namespace and propagates resolution failures.
Query services expose task name rendering, device plus serial matching, current context membership testing, and bulk active reference acquire and release across proxy members.
Pipe draining services expose an outer entry that takes a pipe with output file plus position and length and flags and actor under pipe lock, and an inner entry that runs the wait and feed loop.
A blocking readability wait is available for pipes and temporarily releases the pipe lock while sleeping.
Namespace file handling provides unlocked_ioctl with compat_ioctl routed to a common dispatcher.
Dentry handling pairs d_dname with d_prune for stashed entries.
Deferred task lookup uses a bundle holding ns_ops with task.
Superblock handling provides statfs with evict_inode plus show_path and drop_inode.
Stashed entry handling pairs init_inode with put_data.
Export handling bundles encode_fh with fh_to_dentry plus open and permission.
Registration uses name with init_fs_context and kill_sb, with name nsfs.
Null directory handling provides llseek with read plus iterate_shared and fsync with lock and flock plus fop_flags, while its superblock provides statfs alone.
File handle carries ns_id with ns_type and ns_inum, and mount info carries size with mnt_ns_id and nr_mounts.
Namespace dentries display as type name followed by numeric identifier in brackets for both dynamic naming and path display.

Fresh inodes set i_private with i_mode plus i_fop and i_ino from the namespace while holding an active reference capable of reviving idle subtrees, and eviction drops the active reference with inode clearing before releasing the namespace.
Mount info export reports the smaller of caller and kernel sizes with identifier and mount count excluding root, failing when the caller copy fails.
Extensible command validation requires matching direction with type and number plus caller size at least the stated minimum.
Neighbor mount iteration requires broad visibility across namespaces while other namespace controls require no extra visibility check here.
Owner queries open the owning user namespace with parent queries opening the parent when defined and failing as invalid otherwise, while type queries return the stored clone tag.
Owner identifier queries apply only to user namespaces and translate the stored owner into the caller context with munging before writing to caller memory.

Pid translations apply only to pid namespaces and map between caller visible and target namespace process and thread group identifiers, reporting search failure when the task is absent or the result is zero.
Mount identifier queries apply only to mount namespaces and share behavior with generic identifier queries to return the sixty four bit namespace identifier to caller memory.
Single mount info queries apply only to mount namespaces and require a caller pointer with at least version zero size before delegating to bounded copy.
Task name rendering prefers a distinct real name when defined and otherwise uses the generic type name with numeric serial, releasing the reference and reporting not found when absent.
Identity matching succeeds exactly when serial equals the given inode number and the nsfs device equals the given device.

Handle encoding rejects parent qualified requests with invalid and advertises latest size when the buffer is too small while capping oversized maxima, otherwise storing identifier with type and serial.

After lookup the decoder derives an owning user namespace for outsiders with pid namespaces additionally requiring a live reaper for insiders, rejecting broad access without visibility and unknown types, then consumes the reference into a path.
Export permission always succeeds because decoding already enforced access, and export open performs a root relative open with caller flags.
Context setup creates a pseudo instance with NSFS_MAGIC and caching disabled via s_d_flags while wiring ops with eops and dops and recording stashed handling in s_fs_info.
Proxy acquire and release cover mnt_ns with uts_ns plus ipc_ns and pid_ns_for_children plus cgroup_ns with net_ns plus time_ns and time_ns_for_children.

Null directories present only dot entries with seeking bounded to size two and dot only iteration, lock attempts report unsupported, reads produce no bytes while writes consume all bytes and splice writes drain through a generic pipe helper that claims full length.

Feeding drains buffers in order with per buffer capping and readiness confirmation through a caller actor, advancing offsets and totals while releasing exhausted buffers and marking writer wakeup until the request is satisfied.
Pipe waiting aborts on pending signals with absent writers or existing progress ending the wait and nonblocking mode reporting unavailability, discarding empty buffers before signaling success.
Readability means occupied or writerless as seen from one atomic snapshot, emptiness compares head and tail, and buffer confirmation delegates when defined and otherwise succeeds.
Writer wakeup orders updates before waking sleepers and async notifications, framing starts with zeroed counts and no pending wakeup and ends by waking only when marked.

The control dispatcher validates the command with visibility, resolves the namespace from the open file, then routes to owner with parent and type plus identifier and pid translation and mount info or neighbor iteration handling.
Current membership testing routes on the stored clone tag to the matching per type check across configured types and reports false with a warning for unknown tags.
Early setup mounts the internal instance with panic on failure, clears the no user restriction, and records root mount and dentry for global use.

Neighbor iteration moves from type and size checks to sequential selection to path materialization consuming the reference to descriptor preparation to optional info fill and finally to publication, propagating failures at each move.

Handle decoding moves from length and trailing zero and kind checks to identifier and paired field checks to RCU lookup with consistency and liveness verification and then to ownership and visibility enforcement before path return.
Inner splicing moves from counter init through repeated wait and feed cycles with cooperative rescheduling to final wakeup, returning moved bytes or the terminal status when nothing moved.
Pid translations and handle lookup hold read side RCU across task or namespace lookup and use of the result.
Pipe transfers hold the pipe lock across buffer inspection and actor calls, dropping it only while sleeping for readability and reacquiring before continuing.
Liveness checking without an active reference can race with deactivation yet remains benign because later initialization revives the subtree.

Caller memory writes can fail the operation with undersized or null info requests rejected as invalid, while splice waits can abort on signals or failed confirmation with a specific no data outcome treated as benign end.

Fixed control names are NS_GET_USERNS with NS_GET_PARENT and NS_GET_NSTYPE plus NS_GET_OWNER_UID and NS_GET_MNTNS_ID with NS_GET_ID plus NS_GET_PID_FROM_PIDNS and NS_GET_TGID_FROM_PIDNS with NS_GET_PID_IN_PIDNS and NS_GET_TGID_IN_PIDNS.
Extensible control names are NS_MNT_GET_INFO with NS_MNT_GET_NEXT and NS_MNT_GET_PREV, gated by minimum size MNT_NS_INFO_SIZE_VER0.

Handle word sizes NSFS_FID_SIZE_U32_VER0 and NSFS_FID_SIZE_U32_LATEST derive from byte sizes NSFS_FILE_HANDLE_SIZE_VER0 and NSFS_FILE_HANDLE_SIZE_LATEST, with handle kinds FILEID_NSFS and FILEID_INVALID.

Type tags CLONE_NEWCGROUP with CLONE_NEWIPC and CLONE_NEWNS plus CLONE_NEWNET and CLONE_NEWPID with CLONE_NEWTIME and CLONE_NEWUSER plus CLONE_NEWUTS govern membership with decoding and control dispatch.
Observed failure codes include ENOENT with EINVAL and EPERM plus ESRCH and EFAULT with ENOTTY and ENOIOCTLCMD plus EOPNOTSUPP and ENOMEM with EAGAIN and ERESTARTSYS plus ENOLCK.
Observed flags include O_CLOEXEC with O_RDONLY and SPLICE_F_NONBLOCK.
Filesystem constants include NSFS_MAGIC with DCACHE_DONTCACHE and SB_NOUSER plus S_IRUGO and FOP_IMMUTABLE.
